definition: The Arabic Speech Corpus is a Modern Standard Arabic (MSA) speech corpus for speech synthesis.
details: The corpus contains phonetic and orthographic transcriptions of more than 3.7 hours of MSA speech aligned with recorded speech on the phoneme level. The annotations include word stress marks on the individual phonemes. The Arabic Speech Corpus was built as part of a doctoral project by Nawar Halabi at the University of Southampton funded by MicroLinkPC who own an exclusive license to commercialise the corpus, but the corpus is available for strictly non-commercial purposes through the official Arabic Speech Corpus website. It is distributed under the Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-ShareAlike 4.0 International License.

explainer.lead: The Arabic Speech Corpus is a collection of Modern Standard Arabic recordings with detailed text and sound annotations for building speech synthesizers. Its phoneme-level timing and stress marks help connect written Arabic to the way it is spoken, although use is restricted to non-commercial purposes.

tiers.eli5: Imagine someone reading Arabic aloud while another person labels every tiny sound and shows exactly when it happens. A computer can use those examples to learn how to speak Arabic, a bit like learning to sing by following both the words and the music.
tiers.practitioner: Use the recordings alongside their orthographic and phonetic transcriptions, phoneme-level alignments, and phoneme stress annotations when developing MSA speech synthesis. The corpus is licensed CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 and is strictly non-commercial; MicroLinkPC holds the exclusive commercialisation licence, and the recordings should not be treated as coverage of Arabic dialects.
tiers.paperLevel: Formally, the corpus can be represented as C = {(audio, orthographic transcription, phonetic transcription, phoneme alignment, stress marks)}, containing more than 3.7 hours of Modern Standard Arabic speech. It was built as part of Nawar Halabi’s doctoral project at the University of Southampton, funded by MicroLinkPC; its scope is MSA, and distribution under CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 restricts use to non-commercial purposes.

explainer.example: A researcher selecting 60 minutes from the corpus would use less than 27% of its audio: 60 / (3.7 × 60) ≈ 0.270, and the actual percentage is smaller because the full corpus contains more than 3.7 hours. Each selected recording can be matched with its transcriptions, phoneme boundaries, and stress annotations.

explainer.measures: This is a speech dataset rather than a scoring system, so it does not measure synthesizer quality with a numerical score. It records more than 3.7 hours of MSA speech and describes each recording through text, phonetic symbols, phoneme timing, and stress marks.
